agent: main (CTO mode — controlled protocol amendment, final pre-execution artifact)

constitution_recertification.note: Controlled amendment round. No OX Alpha calls. No new invention work. The sole purpose is to fix 4 methodological problems identified by the CEO before any data is collected. This amendment is issued BEFORE data collection — it does not change the hypothesis, only the statistical and experimental framework that protects the falsification's integrity.

ceo_round_69_audit_summary.ceo_verdict: The protocol-freeze is a major improvement. The machine has finally stopped modifying the invention hypothesis and frozen the experimental question before data collection. That is exactly the right move. But I would not authorize the experiment exactly as currently frozen. There are several statistical and experimental weaknesses that should be corrected before the first sample is collected.
ceo_p0_amendments_required_before_execut: 1. COMPOSITION REQUIREMENT: Require the signal to reproduce in BOTH pre-specified clot compositions to advance the general hypothesis. The current '>=60% in at least ONE composition' allows RBC-rich positive + fibrin-rich completely negative and still advances — that contradicts the cross-composition robustness objective.

2. TIME-SERIES MULTIPLICITY: 15 features x Bonferroni is not enough. Features are evaluated over many time windows (100ms sliding window stepped every 10ms = many opportunities for noise excursion). 15 features != 15 statistical tests. Replace with a frozen time-series inference procedure (block/permutation preserving temporal structure, testing earliest lead-time event as unit of inference).

3. THRESHOLD VS SIGNIFICANCE: 3-sigma/3x baseline is being treated as significance incorrectly. These are signal-detection thresholds, NOT inferential p-values. The variance estimate, baseline stationarity, autocorrelation, and non-Gaussian behavior of force data all matter. Define them separately: 3-sigma = detection threshold; permutation test = inferential test.

4. CONTROL INTERPRETATION: Gelatin controls test instrumentation artifacts, NOT biological specificity. A signal appearing in gelatin tells us it is not completely material-specific. It does NOT establish that a signal observed in thrombus is specifically a pre-fracture biological/mechanical signature. State this explicitly.
ceo_strategic_guidance: Do NOT increase sample size yet. Run the small Stage-0 pilot precisely as a falsification experiment. If it produces nothing, you're done. If it produces a signal, THEN design the adequately powered Stage-1 experiment. Keeps invention cost near zero until reality gives you a reason to spend.
Stage 0 = signal-discovery pilot, not validation. Frame it explicitly as such.
A positive Stage-0 signal does NOT make Slot 5 an invention. It only earns the right to run Stage 1.
The experiment must be cheap enough to kill the idea before you become emotionally or financially committed to it.
ceo_round_69_audit_summary.ceo_competitive_landscape_note: A 2025 patent (US20250186070A1) already describes force/pressure sensing at the catheter tip and using measured clot characteristics such as fragility, stiffness and adherence to influence the aspiration state. A 2025 Nature report describes mechanically modifying clot microstructure. The field is moving rapidly. Even a positive Stage-0 signal does not make Slot 5 an invention.

controlled_amendment.amendment_principle: This amendment is issued BEFORE data collection. It does NOT change the hypothesis (Does a measurable signal reliably precede clot fragmentation by >=1 second?). It fixes 4 methodological problems in the statistical and experimental framework. Per Article XXVII (no threshold invention), all amended thresholds are pre-registered and cannot be adjusted post-hoc.

amendment_1_composition_requirement.problem: The frozen success criterion (Round 69) allowed the signal to succeed in '>=60% of fragmenting clots within at least ONE composition group.' This permits RBC-rich = positive + fibrin-rich = completely negative, and the candidate still advances. That contradicts the original cross-composition robustness objective.
amendment_1_composition_requirement.amendment: The precursor must be observed in BOTH pre-specified composition groups to advance the general hypothesis. Specifically: at least ONE frozen feature must show significant deviation (per the amended time-series inference procedure, Amendment 2) before t_fragmentation in >=60% of fragmenting clots within EACH composition group (RBC-rich AND fibrin-rich).
amendment_1_composition_requirement.if_signal_in_only_one_composition: If the signal appears in only one composition group, the result is composition-specific. This does NOT kill the candidate but does NOT advance the general hypothesis. Instead, it generates a narrower composition-specific hypothesis that must be tested in a separate Stage-1 experiment with adequate power for that composition only. The general cross-composition candidate remains at DISCOVERY_HYPOTHESIS status.
amendment_1_composition_requirement.revised_kill_condition_K0_4: K0_4 (not reproducible): If a feature deviates before fragmentation in some trials but not others, AND the pattern does not reproduce across BOTH composition groups (i.e., significant in one composition but not the other), the GENERAL cross-composition hypothesis is not supported. Record as COMPOSITION-SPECIFIC SIGNAL — does not advance general candidate but does not kill it either. Triggers Stage-1 design for the specific composition.

amendment_2_time_series_multiplicity.problem: The frozen protocol (Round 69) applied Bonferroni correction across 15 features (0.05/15 = 0.0033). But several features are evaluated over many time windows (100ms sliding window stepped every 10ms = ~100 windows per 10s trial). This creates a much larger multiple-comparisons problem: 15 features x ~100 windows = ~1500 tests per clot. Simple Bonferroni across features does not control for temporal multiplicity.
amendment_2_time_series_multiplicity.amendment: Replace the simple '15 features x Bonferroni' logic with a FROZEN TIME-SERIES INFERENCE PROCEDURE:

procedure.step_1: For each feature, compute the time series of the feature value across the entire trial (sliding 100ms window, stepped at 10ms intervals).
procedure.step_2: For each feature, define the 'earliest deviation time' as the first time point at which the feature crosses its detection threshold (3-sigma for force/displacement magnitude; 3x baseline for derivative/HF/stiffness). This is a SINGLE event per feature per trial, not a per-window test.
procedure.step_3: The UNIT OF INFERENCE is the earliest deviation event, NOT the per-window crossing. The question is: 'Does the earliest deviation time precede t_fragmentation by >=1.0 second?' — a single binary outcome per feature per trial.
procedure.step_4: INFERENTIAL TEST: Block permutation test. For each feature, under the null hypothesis (no relationship between feature deviation and fragmentation), the earliest deviation time is equally likely to occur at any point in the trial. Permute the deviation time relative to t_fragmentation across all fragmenting trials (1000 permutations, stratified by composition group). Compute the p-value for the observed lead time.
procedure.step_5: MULTIPLE COMPARISON CORRECTION: Apply Bonferroni correction across the 15 features (0.05/15 = 0.0033) on the PERMUTATION p-value (not on per-window crossings). This correctly controls family-wise error because the unit of inference is the feature-level event, not the window-level crossing.
procedure.step_6: REPORT: For each of the 15 features, report: (a) earliest deviation time per trial, (b) lead time per trial, (c) permutation p-value, (d) Bonferroni-corrected significance, (e) proportion of fragmenting clots with significant lead time, per composition group. Report ALL 15 features, including non-significant ones.

amendment_2_time_series_multiplicity.key_distinction: The detection threshold (3-sigma) identifies WHEN a feature deviates. The permutation test determines WHETHER that deviation is statistically associated with subsequent fragmentation. These are separate questions with separate answers.

amendment_3_threshold_vs_significance.problem: The frozen protocol (Round 69) treated '3-sigma deviation' as equivalent to statistical significance. This is incorrect. 3-sigma is a signal-detection threshold; it identifies when a feature value exceeds a noise baseline. It does NOT test whether that exceedance is statistically associated with a subsequent event (fragmentation). The variance estimate, baseline stationarity, autocorrelation, and non-Gaussian behavior of force data all affect whether a 3-sigma crossing is meaningful.

detection_threshold.definition: A pre-specified criterion for identifying when a feature value deviates from its baseline. This is a SIGNAL-DETECTION tool, not an inferential test.

values.force_magnitude: F(t) deviates from F_baseline by >3 standard deviations of the baseline period (first 1s after traction onset)
values.force_derivative: |dF/dt| exceeds 3x the mean |dF/dt| of the baseline period

detection_threshold.purpose: To identify the EARLIEST DEVIATION TIME for each feature — the time point at which the feature first crosses its detection threshold. This time is then used as the input to the inferential test.
detection_threshold.not_a_p_value: Crossing a 3-sigma threshold does NOT imply p<0.0033. The 3-sigma threshold is a detection rule, not a significance test. A feature can cross 3-sigma by chance (especially with autocorrelated time-series data). The inferential question is answered by the permutation test (Amendment 2).

inferential_test.definition: A block permutation test (Amendment 2, step 4) that tests whether the earliest deviation time is statistically associated with subsequent fragmentation. This IS an inferential test with a p-value.
inferential_test.significance_threshold: Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.0033 (0.05/15 features) on the permutation p-value.
inferential_test.relationship_to_detection_threshold: The detection threshold identifies WHEN. The permutation test determines WHETHER. A feature must pass BOTH: (a) cross its detection threshold at some time before t_fragmentation, AND (b) have a permutation p-value < 0.0033 for the association between deviation time and fragmentation time.

amendment_4_control_interpretation.problem: The frozen protocol (Round 69) used gelatin/agar phantoms as negative controls and stated that if features show deviation in gelatin trials, the signal is an artifact (K0_5). But gelatin controls only test whether the APPARATUS creates a generic false signal. They do NOT reproduce clot viscoelasticity, vessel-wall interaction, device engagement, or traction-induced deformation. A signal appearing in gelatin tells us it is not completely material-specific, but it does NOT establish that a signal observed in thrombus is specifically a pre-fracture biological/mechanical signature.
amendment_4_control_interpretation.amendment: State explicitly the scope and limitation of the gelatin control:
amendment_4_control_interpretation.gelatin_control_tests: INSTRUMENTATION ARTIFACTS ONLY. Gelatin controls verify that the force sensor, displacement encoder, and camera do not produce false-positive fracture signatures when no biological material is present. If features deviate in gelatin trials, the signal is an apparatus artifact (K0_5 fires).
gelatin_control_does_NOT_test: Biological specificity (whether the signal is unique to thrombus vs other viscoelastic materials)
Pre-fracture mechanical specificity (whether the signal reflects clot mechanical failure vs other clot-state changes)
Vessel-wall interaction effects (gelatin in a tube does not reproduce clot-vessel adhesion)
Device engagement specificity (gelatin may engage the device differently than clot)
Clinical realism (gelatin is not a validated thrombus analog)
amendment_4_control_interpretation.additional_control_recommended_for_stage: If Stage 0 produces a positive signal, Stage 1 should include: (a) non-fragmenting thrombus trials (clot successfully removed without fragmentation — serves as within-experiment biological control), (b) different thrombus analogs (e.g., fibrin-only gels, RBC-suspended gels) to test biological specificity, (c) vessel-wall interaction tests (clot in curved vessel with compliant wall).
amendment_4_control_interpretation.revised_K0_5_interpretation: K0_5 fires if features deviate in gelatin negative-control trials. K0_5 does NOT fire if features deviate only in thrombus trials — that is the expected result. But a positive thrombus-only signal must be interpreted narrowly: 'the signal is not an apparatus artifact, but its biological specificity is untested in Stage 0.'

stage_0_framing.framing: SIGNAL-DISCOVERY PILOT — not validation. Stage 0 is designed to answer ONE question: Does any measurable signal precede fragmentation by >=1 second? It is NOT designed to: (a) estimate sensitivity/specificity with clinical precision, (b) generalize across clot compositions with statistical power, (c) establish clinical utility, (d) prove the signal is biologically specific to pre-fracture state.
stage_0_framing.sample_size_justification: 5 clots per composition (10 total) is sufficient for a FALSIFICATION PILOT. If no signal exists in ANY of the 10 clots, the hypothesis is killed at minimal cost. If a signal exists, the pilot is not powered to estimate its prevalence — it only justifies spending more money on a properly powered Stage-1 experiment.
stage_0_framing.if_positive: A positive Stage-0 result earns the right to design Stage 1 (adequately powered, out-of-sample prediction, robustness across conditions). It does NOT make Slot 5 an invention.
stage_0_framing.if_negative: A negative Stage-0 result kills the candidate. Record CE-019. Slot 5 EMPTY.

amended_kill_conditions_summary.K0_1_no_fragmentation: If <3 clots fragment across all trials, experiment is inconclusive (not enough fragmentation events). Re-design with more friable compositions or more aggressive traction. NOT a kill of the hypothesis.
amended_kill_conditions_summary.K0_2_no_signal: If NO feature (across all 15) shows BOTH (a) detection-threshold crossing before t_fragmentation AND (b) permutation p-value <0.0033, in ANY fragmenting clot, the pre-fragmentation signal does not exist. KILL. Record CE-019.
amended_kill_conditions_summary.K0_3_lead_time_too_short: If features pass detection + permutation but median lead time across fragmenting clots is <1.0 second, the signal exists but is too early to act on. KILL. Record CE-019.
amended_kill_conditions_summary.K0_4_not_reproducible_or_composition_spe: If signal appears in only ONE composition group: COMPOSITION-SPECIFIC SIGNAL. Does NOT advance general candidate. Does NOT kill. Triggers Stage-1 design for that composition only. If signal appears in NEITHER composition group: KILL. Record CE-019.
amended_kill_conditions_summary.K0_5_confounded_by_apparatus: If features deviate in gelatin negative-control trials: apparatus artifact. KILL. Record CE-019. NOTE: gelatin controls test instrumentation artifacts ONLY — they do NOT establish biological specificity of a thrombus-only signal.

amended_success_criteria.to_advance_general_candidate_to_stage_1: ALL of the following: (a) at least ONE of 15 features passes BOTH detection threshold AND permutation test (p<0.0033) in fragmenting clots, (b) median lead time >=1.0 second, (c) signal reproduces in BOTH composition groups (>=60% of fragmenting clots in EACH group), (d) NO deviation in gelatin negative controls.
amended_success_criteria.to_generate_composition_specific_hypothe: Signal appears in ONE composition group only. Does NOT advance general candidate. Triggers Stage-1 design for that composition. General candidate remains at DISCOVERY_HYPOTHESIS.
amended_success_criteria.to_kill: ANY of K0_2, K0_3, K0_5 fires. OR signal appears in NEITHER composition group (K0_4 general kill).
